text:
maya: Anyone running into a weird import/interop issue with the JS SDK on Vite + Edge runtime? Works in Node but edge deploy gets a runtime error.

sahil: I hit something similar last week with a different lib. Can you paste a minimal repro?

maya: Repro steps I used:
1) node 18, pnpm
2) simple vite app (latest) + @vercel/edge-runtime (or Cloudflare Pages)
3) package.json has "type": "module" and SDK installed as "redwood-js-sdk@0.15.0"
4) entry: `import Redwood from 'redwood-js-sdk'`
5) build succeeds but runtime (edge) fails with:
```
ReferenceError: require is not defined
    at file:///workspace/.netlify/functions/edge/handler.js:12:15
    at ModuleJob.run (node:internal/modules/esm/module_job:194:25
```
and TS in editor shows: "TS1259: Module '\"redwood-js-sdk\"' can only be default-imported using the 'esModuleInterop' flag."

nick: That stack looks like the bundle has a CJS pattern left in (uses `require`) while the runtime expects pure ESM. Vite sometimes prebundles deps as CJS if it can't find an ESM entry or the package.json exports map is ambiguous.

maya: Confirmed: when I `node -e "console.log(require('redwood-js-sdk'))"` in a local Node CJS script, it prints the SDK object. The published package seems to expose CJS in some paths.

olivia: Could also be types vs runtime mismatch — if the SDK ships `types` pointing at a d.ts that uses `export =`, editors will complain unless consumers set `esModuleInterop`.

maya: Minimal package.json from repro:
```json
{
  "name": "edge-repro",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": {
    "redwood-js-sdk": "0.15.0"
  }
}
```
vite.config.js snippet:
```js
export default {
  build: { target: 'es2022' },
  optimizeDeps: { include: ['redwood-js-sdk'] }
}
```

sahil: Two quick workarounds to unblock apps: 1) import namespace: `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-js-sdk'` or 2) enable esModuleInterop/allowSyntheticDefaultImports in tsconfig (not ideal for prod).

nick: Long-term fix for SDK package: add explicit conditional exports in package.json so bundlers pick the ESM entry for modern environments and a CJS entry for legacy. Example suggestion:
```json
"exports": {
  "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
  "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
  "default": "./dist/esm/index.js"
},
"type": "module",
"main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
"module": "dist/esm/index.js",
"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"
```

olivia: Also check that the ESM build does not emit `module.exports =` anywhere (some bundlers will wrap). We should run a smoke on edge runtimes (Cloudflare, Vercel Edge) before cutting releases.

maya: Repro repo uploaded to https://github.com/maya/edge-sdk-repro (private link in DM) — includes `pnpm build` + edge deploy script that fails.

dev-bot: Created issue #342 (redwood-js-sdk: exports map + typings causing bundler edge breakage) and linked repo.

sahil: For the PR we should: 1) add conditional exports as above, 2) verify typings use `export default` style or ship interop d.ts to avoid TS1259, 3) add CI job that runs Vite + Esbuild build and a tiny edge function smoke test in Node 18+ edge emulation.

nick: For Vite-specific advice in the meantime: set `optimizeDeps: { esbuildOptions: { target: 'esnext' } }` and `ssr: { noExternal: ['redwood-js-sdk'] }` so Vite forces ESM resolution and bundles the ESM entry. That made the repro app work locally for me.

maya: Thanks — that unblocked our demo. I'll open the PR with suggested package.json exports and attach the failing bundle snapshot.

olivia: Assigning to @devex for follow-up QA once PR lands.

maya: :thumbsup:
